defects_found.description: The six source-<celex>.txt archive files hold only narrow ~600-900-char cited-excerpt windows (2-12KB total per file) around each FACT claim's offsets, not the full fetched documents (43,813-178,953 chars each) — even though window.__docs[celex].length confirmed each full document was actually fetched into page memory.
defects_found.root_cause: javascript_tool's return-value channel truncates to roughly 1.0-1.5K characters regardless of the requested slice size (a 20,000-char or even 3,000-char return is silently cut off mid-string with a [TRUNCATED] marker, no error) — the MINT-RUNBOOK.md-suggested '20000-char substrings per call' does not work as written. Worked around this batch via small indexOf/regex offset probes plus small (~600-900-char) windowed returns, i.e. a deliberate targeted-excerpt strategy, not a full-document dump.

defects_found.description: Two transcription bugs were introduced while manually copying cited spans into source-<celex>.txt / payload FACT claims: an ASCII 'x' substituted for the source's real '×' (multiplication sign) in 32019R1242's Article 8 excerpt and jurisdictional_scope span; curly quotation marks ('...') substituted for the source's straight quotes around 'CBAM' in 32023R0956.
defects_found.root_cause: manual transcription during the targeted-excerpt copying described in defects_found[0]; neither bug was caught until the independent verbatim cross-check against the archived source file (BATCH-001-REPORT-v2.md §4-5).
defects_found.fix_ref: corrected in-session before BATCH-001-REPORT-v2.md was reported green — a process/verification fix, not a code fix

defects_found.description: validate-mint-payload.mjs's criterion 3 (fact_span_not_in_source) only checks internal self-consistency between a payload's own result_content and source_span fields; it does not compare either against the independently archived primary-source file. The 32019R1242 × → x substitution was present identically in both fields, so it passed the validator clean while silently diverging from the real fetched text — a payload can be internally self-consistent yet not truly verbatim.
defects_found.root_cause: the kit's validator (a $0, in-session proxy for the live validate_item_provenance RPC, per MINT-RUNBOOK.md §5) has no unicode-normalization or external-source comparison step; its scope is intra-payload only.
